([[Delafield, Wisconsin]]) | college = * [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] (2021–2022) * [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara]] (2022–2023) | draft_year = 2023 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 19 | draft_team = [[Golden State Warriors]] | career_start = 2023 | years1 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–present | team1 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]] | team2 = →[[Santa Cruz Warriors]] | highlights = * [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie First Team]] ({{nbay|2023|end}}) * [[West Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|WCC co-Player of the Year]] (2023) * First-team All-[[West Coast Conference|WCC]] (2023) * WCC Newcomer of the Year (2023) * [[Wisconsin Mr. Basketball]] (2021) }} '''Brandin''' '''Thomas''' '''Podziemski''' ({{IPAc-en|p|ə|ˈ|d|ʒ|ɛ|m|s|k|i}} {{respelling|pə|JEM|skee}};{{cite press release |title=Golden State Warriors 2024-25 pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/golden-state-warriors-2024-25-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |access-date=Feb 8, 2025}} born February 25, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). A guard, he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois Fighting Illini]] and the [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara Broncos.]] Podziemski was chosen by the Warriors with the 19th pick in the 2023 NBA draft. He is nicknamed "'''Podz'''".{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/podzibr01.html|title=Brandon Podziemski|website=BasketballReference.com}} Known for his hustle and three-point shooting, he is considered one of the best young players in the NBA. {{Cite web |date=2024-10-24 |title=25-under-25: Brandin Podziemski is the future of Warriors basketball |url=https://fansided.com/brandin-podziemski-nba-player-rankings-warriors-2025 |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=FanSided |language=en-US}} ==Early life and high school career== Podziemski grew up in [[Greenfield, Wisconsin]] and attended [[St. John's Northwestern Military Academy]].{{cite web|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/high-schools/2021/01/28/how-brandin-podziemski-became-top-basketbal-recruit-wisconsin/4275354001/|title=How Brandin Podziemski became a top basketball recruit in Wisconsin|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=January 28, 2021|access-date=January 23, 2023}} He was named first-team All-State after averaging 22.5 points and 9.3 rebounds per game as a sophomore with [[St. John's Northwestern Military Academy]] after not playing on the varsity team as a freshman at [[Muskego High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/high-schools/2020/02/06/brandin-podziemski-more-than-just-shooter-st-johns-basketball/4675625002/|title=Brandin Podziemski is 'more than just a shooter' for St. John's basketball|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=February 6, 2020|access-date=January 23, 2023}} Podziemski averaged 27.6 points and 9.2 rebounds and repeated as a first-team All-State selection during his junior season.{{cite web|url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-recruiting/article248960134.html|title=Brandin Podziemski proving himself as a top recruit. What's next for the UK target?|work=[[Lexington Herald Leader]]|date=February 3, 2021|access-date=January 23, 2023}} He was named [[Wisconsin Mr. Basketball]]{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Mark |date=March 6, 2021 |title=St. John's Northwestern's Brandin Podziemski selected as 2021 Mr. Basketball by WBCA |url=https://www.wissports.net/news_article/show/1149953-st-john-s-northwestern-s-brandin-podziemski-selected-as-2021-mr-basketball-by-wbca |access-date=January 16, 2024 |website=Wisconsin High School Sports {{!}} Wisconsin Sports Network {{!}} WisSports.net |language=en-us}} as a senior after averaging 35.1 points, ten rebounds, 5.6 assists, and four steals per game.{{cite web|access-date=January 23, 2023|date=March 6, 2021|title=Brandin Podziemski named 2021 Wisconsin Mr. Basketball recipient|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/high-schools/2021/03/06/brandin-podziemski-named-2021-wisconsin-mr-basketball-recipient/4610342001/|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]}} Podziemski was also named the boys basketball Gatorade Player of the Year for Wisconsin in 2021.{{Cite web |title=Brandin Podziemski 2020 - 2021 WISCONSIN BOYS BASKETBALL PLAYER OF THE YEAR |url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/brandin-podziemski/38381#! |access-date=January 16, 2024 |website=playeroftheyear.gatorade.com}} Podziemski was rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing college basketball for [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] over offers from [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (FL)]], [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]], and [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]].{{cite web|url=https://www.news-gazette.com/sports/update-podziemski-embraced-challenge-secured-big-ten-opportunity/article_46eb014d-9d88-5ae3-b90c-7b19581f178a.html|title=Podziemski embraced challenge, secured Big Ten opportunity|work=[[The News-Gazette (Champaign–Urbana)|The News-Gazette]]|date=April 13, 2021|access-date=January 23, 2023}} ==College career== Podziemski began his college basketball career with the [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois Fighting Illini]].{{cite web|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/college/article/Santa-Clara-s-star-guard-went-from-Illinois-17726185.php|title=Santa Clara's star guard went from Illinois' bench to one of WCC's best in a year|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|date=January 20, 2023|access-date=January 23, 2023 |last1=Kroner |first1=Steve }} He played in 16 games as a freshman, all off the bench, and averaged 1.4 points per game. After the end of the season, Podziemski entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]].{{cite web|url=http://www.news-gazette.com/sports/report-podziemski-in-portal/article_884082b9-3a6f-594f-85c0-590b51a62147.html|title=Podziemski in portal|first=Scott|last=Richey|work=[[The News-Gazette (Champaign–Urbana)|The News-Gazette]]|date=April 12, 2022|access-date=January 23, 2023}} Podziemski ultimately transferred to [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara]].{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/illinois/Article/Former-Illinois-guard-Brandin-Podziemski-commits-to-Santa-Clara-basktball-NCAA-Transfer-Portal-187263436/|title=Former Illini guard Brandin Podziemski commits to Santa Clara|first=Joey|last=Wagner|website=[[247Sports]]|date=May 6, 2022|access-date=January 23, 2023}} He entered his first season with the Broncos as the team's starting shooting guard.{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2023/jan/06/gonzaga-santa-clara-key-matchup-broncos-guard-bran/|title=Gonzaga-Santa Clara key matchup: Broncos guard Brandin Podziemski enjoying breakout season|first=Jim|last=Meehan|work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|date=January 7, 2023|access-date=January 23, 2023}} After scoring only 22 points during his entire season at Illinois, Podziemski scored 30 points with 9 rebounds and 5 steals in Santa Clara's season opener against [[2022–23 Eastern Washington Eagles men's basketball team|Eastern Washington]] as the Broncos won 84–72.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401488780|title=Podziemski scores 30 to lead Santa Clara past EWU 84-72|website=[[ESPN.com]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 8, 2022|access-date=March 1, 2023}} He scored 34 points and grabbed 11 rebounds in the following game against [[2022–23 Georgia Southern Eagles men's basketball team|Georgia Southern]].At the close of the 2022–23 regular season, he was named WCC co-Player of the Year, sharing the award with [[Drew Timme]] of [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], WCC Newcomer of the Year, NABC First Team, USBWA All-District, and All-WCC First Team.{{Cite web |title=Brandin Podziemski - 2022-23 - Men's Basketball |url=https://santaclarabroncos.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/brandin-podziemski/7673 |access-date=January 16, 2024 |website=Santa Clara University |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=March 1, 2023 |title=WCC Announces 2022-23 Men's Basketball All-Conference Awards |url=https://wccsports.com/news/2023/2/25/athlete-awards-wcc-announces-2022-23-mens-basketball-all-conference-awards.aspx |access-date=January 16, 2024 |website=wccsports.com |language=en}}{{cite web|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/college/article/santa-clara-s-brandin-podziemski-named-wcc-17813844.php|title=Santa Clara's Brandin Podziemski named WCC Co-Player of the Year|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|date=March 1, 2023|access-date=March 1, 2023 |last1=Kroner |first1=Steve }} Podziemski also earned WCC Player of the Week honors a SCU record four times, his 636 points was the fourth most in a season in program history, and his SCU three-point percentage was fourth-best in SCU program history. Podziemski was one of only three NCAA Division 1 men's basketball players to average 19, 8, and 3 in the 2022–23 season and finished 5th in the nation in three-point field goal percentage (43.8%).{{Cite web |date=June 23, 2023 |title=Warriors Select Guard Brandin Podziemski With 19th Overall Pick in 2023 NBA Draft, Presented by HPE |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-select-guard-brandin-podziemski-with-19th-overall-pick-20230622 |access-date=January 16, 2024 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} Podziemski declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]] while maintaining his eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2023/03/22/santa-clara-standout-brandin-podziemski-declares-for-nba-draft|title=Santa Clara standout Brandin Podziemski declares for NBA Draft|work=[[The Mercury News]]|date=March 22, 2023|access-date=March 24, 2023}} After taking part in the [[NBA Draft Combine]] and receiving positive feedback, he decided to remain in the draft.{{cite web|url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article275655901.html|title=Brandin Podziemski talks NBA Draft, almost picking Kentucky|work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]|date=May 23, 2023|access-date=June 23, 2023}} ==Professional career== The [[Golden State Warriors]] selected Podziemski with the nineteenth overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Steve|last=Kroner|title=Who is Brandin Podziemski, the Warriors' 2023 first-round draft pick?|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/warriors/article/brandin-podziemski-warriors-2023-first-round-18160152.php|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|date=June 22, 2023|access-date=June 23, 2023}} On July 3, 2023, the Warriors signed him to a contract.{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign 2023 First Round Draft Pick Brandin Podziemski|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-2023-first-round-draft-pick-brandin-podziemski-20230703|website=NBA.com|date=July 3, 2023|access-date=September 26, 2023}} Podziemski plays the guard position.{{Cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/videos/brandin-podziemski-highlights-watch-warriors-141754523.html|title=Brandin Podziemski highlights: Watch Warriors guard score 22 in loss to Clippers|date=March 3, 2026|website=Yahoo Sports}} On December 12, 2023, against the [[Phoenix Suns]], Podziemski became the first [[Golden State Warriors]] rookie to have 20 or more points, 10 or more rebounds (11), and five or more assists in a single game since two-time NBA MVP [[Stephen Curry]] did so in the 2009–10 season.{{Cite web |title=Brandin Podziemski '21 Sets Rookie Milestone for Warriors |url=https://sjnacademies.org/news/brandin-podziemski-21-sets-rookie-milestone-for-warriors/ |access-date=January 16, 2024 |website=St. John's Northwestern Academies |language=en-US}} On May 21, 2024, Podziemski was announced on the NBA all-rookie first team. Before the [[Olympic Games]], he was drafted to the USA Select Team alongside his teammate [[Trayce Jackson-Davis]].{{Cite web |date=July 11, 2024 |title=Warriors' Podziemski, Jackson-Davis reflect on USA Select Team experience: 'We brought it to them' |url=https://www.thereporter.com/2024/07/11/warriors-podziemski-jackson-davis-reflect-on-usa-select-team-experience-we-brought-it-to-them/ |access-date=August 26, 2024 |website=The Vacaville Reporter |language=en-US}} On December 28, 2024, during the Warriors' 109–105 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]], Podziemski suffered an abdominal injury in the second quarter. He missed 12 straight games due to the injury. Podziemski returned on January 23, 2025, recording 10 points and four rebounds in a blowout win against the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite web |last=Hardee |first=Daniel |date=2025-01-23 |title=Brandin Podziemski makes his return tonight against Chicago Bulls |url=https://www.goldenstateofmind.com/2025/1/23/24350619/nba-2025-news-injury-golden-state-warriors-brandin-podziemski-stephen-curry-chicago-bulls |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=Golden State Of Mind |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2025-01-17 |title=Podz takes big step in injury recovery, but out for Warriors-Wizards |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/podz-takes-big-step-injury-141232894.html |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}} On February 5, 2025, Podziemski tallied a then career-high 29 points, along with six rebounds and four assists, in a 131–128 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{Cite web |date=2025-02-05 |title=What we learned as Warriors' emotional day ends with collapse vs. Jazz |url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/nba/golden-state-warriors/brandin-podziemski-steph-curry-jazz/1826219/ |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=NBC Sports Bay Area & California |language=en-US}} On February 8, the NBA announced that Podziemski would play in their [[Rising Stars Challenge|Rising Stars]] game as an injury replacement player for [[Cason Wallace]].{{cite web|title=Brandin Podziemski Named to 2025 Rising Stars Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/brandin-podziemski-named-to-2025-rising-stars-roster|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}} On February 23, Podziemski recorded 17 points along with a then career-high 13 rebounds in a 126–102 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]], notching his first [[double-double]] of the season.{{Cite web |title=NBA Fantasy Basketball News |url=https://www.rotowire.com/basketball/news.php |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=www.rotowire.com}} On May 14, he scored a playoff career-high 28 points in a 121–110 closeout loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in Game 5 of the Conference Semifinals.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401769987|title=Timberwolves beat Warriors in Game 5 to reach Western Conference finals for 2nd straight year|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=May 15, 2025|access-date=May 15, 2025}} On May 28, 2025, Podziemski underwent a successful left wrist [[debridement]] surgery.{{Cite web|title=Brandon Podziemski Undergoes Successful Surgery|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/brandin-podziemski-undergoes-successful-surgery-20250528|access-date=July 21, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}} On June 12, Podziemski underwent an additional surgery to repair a core muscle injury.{{Cite web|title=Warriors' Brandin Podziemski has second surgery of offseason|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45496955/warriors-brandon-podziemski-second-surgery-offseason|access-date=September 28, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}} On April 10, 2026, Podziemski recorded a career-high 30 points in a 124–118 loss to the [[2025–26 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/gameday-recap-20260410|title=Brandin Podziemski Scores Career-High 30 Points in Warriors' Loss to Kings|website=nba.com|last=Champion|first=Kalyn|date=April 10, 2026|access-date=April 13, 2026}} He appeared in all 82 games (starting 43) for Golden State during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], averaging 13.8 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 3.7 assists.{{Cite web|title=Here Are The NBA's 2026-26 Iron Men. How Do They Compare To Years Past?|url=https://www.si.com/nba/iron-men-players-all-82-games-list-compared-years-past|access-date=July 31, 2026|website=si.com|language=en}} ==Personal life== Podziemski is of Polish descent and has expressed interest in obtaining Polish citizenship in order to play for the [[Poland men's national basketball team|Poland national team]]. He is being recruited to the team by member [[Jeremy Sochan]].{{cite web | url=https://www.sport.pl/koszykowka/7,64947,29799086,podziemski-moze-trafic-do-nba-i-reprezentacji-polski-nowa-gwiazda.html| title=Podziemski może trafić do NBA i reprezentacji Polski.
